name: esp2024_buoy
story: Waves roll the buoy up to 10 degrees and lift it up and down; the load pin feels each pull of the chain. At 8 s the chain breaks: the pull falls to zero, the alert goes out, the buoy rises and drifts off with the tide while the tracker follows it.

steps.title: Open the Dynamic Simulation environment
steps.command: Environments tab > Begin panel > Dynamic Simulation
actions: Open esp2024_buoy.iam in Inventor.
Click the Environments tab, then Dynamic Simulation.
steps.note: Dynamic Simulation works out how an assembly moves, and the forces and speeds as it moves.

steps.title: Turn constraints into joints
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Settings
actions: Click Simulation Settings and tick Automatically convert constraints to standard joints. Click OK.
Open Standard Joints in the browser to see the joints Inventor made from your assembly constraints.
steps.note: Parts held together with no movement between them become one rigid group, listed under Welded group.

steps.title: Free the buoy
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: In Standard Joints, every part of the buoy above the broken link is one Welded group: the buoy moves as one body.
Delete the grounded constraint on the float and Insert Joint > Spatial (6 degrees of freedom) between the float and the ground, so the buoy can roll, heave and drift.
steps.note: Inventor has no sea, so the wave motion is put in as imposed motion, from the roll and heave worked out on the calculation sheet.

steps.title: Join the chain
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: Insert Joint, Spherical (ball) between the shackle and the swivel and between each pair of links.
Chain links 3 and 4 get their own Spatial joint, so they can fall away when the chain breaks.

steps.title: Roll and heave in the waves
steps.command: Right click the Spatial joint > Properties > Edit imposed motion
actions: dof 5 (rotation about Y): enable imposed motion, Position, a sine wave of 10 degrees amplitude and a 3 s period (use the Input Grapher: Sine).
dof 3 (translation in Z): a sine wave of 40 mm amplitude, the same period.
steps.note: The buoy rolls about its centre of gravity, 756 mm below the waterline. A GM of 229 mm brings it back upright every time.

steps.title: Break the chain at 8 s
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint (suppress at 8 s)
actions: Suppress the joint between chain links 2 and 3 at 8 s (Construct, then right click > Suppress at time).
Links 3 and 4 fall away. Add imposed motion on dof 3: the buoy rises 48 mm as the weight of the hanging chain comes off, then dof 1 (X): it drifts 0.9 m with the tide by 16 s.
steps.note: At the moment the chain breaks the load pin reads zero. The control unit sees this and sends an alert with the GNSS position at once, then reports the position every minute while the buoy drifts.

steps.title: Run the simulation
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Player
actions: In the Simulation Player set Final Time to 16 s and Images to 800.
Click Run. The assembly moves and the timeline fills in.
Use the slider to scrub back and forth.
steps.note: Press Play below to run the same motion here.

steps.title: Plot the results
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Results panel > Output Grapher
actions: Open the Output Grapher.
Under Standard Joints, tick the rotation of the Spatial joint, the force in the shackle joint (the load pin) and the X position.
The graph shows each value against time. Click on the graph to move the simulation to that moment.

steps.title: Record a video
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Player
actions: In the Simulation Player click Record (the red dot) and choose a file name and format.
Click Run again. Inventor saves a video of the motion for your portfolio.
steps.note: You can also export a moment to Stress Analysis (Export to FEA) to check a part at its highest load.
